title: Things to Do in Miami Beach: Three Stops Beyond the Beach Towel
description: Explore Ocean Drive, Lummus Park and South Pointe Park on a Miami Beach outing that goes beyond time on the sand.
body:
Looking for things to do in Miami Beach beyond a few hours on the sand? Ocean Drive, Lummus Park and South Pointe Park make a compact South Beach selection, combining street-facing architecture, a beachfront park and a different view from the island’s southern end.

These stops are in Miami Beach, across the bay from mainland Miami. Keep that distinction in your travel plans if you are staying downtown or adding a mainland neighbourhood to the day.

1. Look up along Ocean Drive

Focus on the public sidewalk between 10th and 8th Streets. This short stretch lets you enjoy the street-facing buildings without needing to enter a hotel or restaurant. The destination’s South Beach guide introduces the area’s architecture and setting.

A smaller section is a useful choice if you want to look closely without spending the afternoon following a long checklist. Take time to see the façades in their street setting, with the park across the way and people moving through the neighbourhood.

Plan the stop: Use public pavement and respect hotel entrances and dining areas. Looking from the street needs no purchase. Event arrangements and traffic patterns can change, so use designated crossings rather than assuming the road is closed.

2. Move into Lummus Park

Lummus Park sits between Ocean Drive and the Atlantic, with paved paths as well as access toward the beach. The City of Miami Beach’s park page lists its location, amenities and current hours.

Near 8th Street, the paved route gives the outing a different feel from the building-lined sidewalk. You can spend time here without making swimming or sunbathing part of the plan. The park offers a way to enjoy the coast while keeping the visit flexible.

Plan the stop: Share paths with other users and leave exercise areas for their intended use. Public restrooms are listed at several street access points, but check what is available when you arrive. Bring drinking water and make a shade or indoor break part of a warm-weather day.

3. Finish at South Pointe Park

At Miami Beach’s southern end, South Pointe Park opens the view toward the ocean and shipping channel. The official destination guide describes the park and its waterfront setting.

Begin at the Washington Avenue entrance and enjoy the open paved areas. There is enough to take in without reaching the pier or waiting for a particular ship. The broad waterfront makes a natural final stop after the closer views along Ocean Drive.

Plan the stop: Park and pier access are distinct. Follow current notices, especially if weather affects the waterfront. This suggestion does not require entering the water or using the pier.

Keep the South Beach plan comfortable

Start with Ocean Drive and Lummus Park, then continue south to South Pointe Park. Allow roughly two to three hours as a flexible time budget including pauses, with more time for food or beach activities.

If walking the connection does not suit the weather or your group, check the city’s current South Beach trolley information before choosing a stop and direction. Do not rely on an old route number. The public-space visits need no attraction ticket; food, transport choices and optional activities are separate. Read our Miami visitor guide for more local context.
